narrative.overview:
This is a calm decision interface where evidence is counted, called, held, or investigated in public view. Warm paper, ink rules, exact mono text, and square fields make it read as an executive evidence record rather than a SaaS dashboard. The title and decision call establish the conclusion before a reader enters the supporting record.

Public observation and synthetic planning are intentionally inequivalent visual states. Solid mint identifies public observed evidence; a labelled, faintly hatched lilac lane identifies synthetic demonstrations. Orange calls attention or carries keyboard focus, while red is held for limitations and warnings.
keyCharacteristics: Warm-paper ground with dark ink rules and a square, flat component language.
Newsreader decision calls paired with IBM Plex Mono throughout operational evidence.
Public and synthetic evidence separated by written labels, hue, and a synthetic-only hatch pattern.
Chart records always paired with a native table alternative and provenance disclosure.

rules.name: The Evidence Lane Rule
rules.body: Never collapse public and synthetic evidence into an unmarked common surface. Public evidence stays solid mint; synthetic evidence stays hatched lilac, and both retain explicit written labels.

rules.name: The Record Type Rule
rules.body: Keep operational UI, numbers, navigation, provenance, and tables in IBM Plex Mono. Use Newsreader for decision statements and evidence headings only.

rules.name: The Flat Record Rule
rules.body: Express hierarchy with rules, contrast, and open space—not rounded cards, shadows, glass, or decorative gradients.

dos: Do lead every route with its decision, next action, and visible evidence boundary.
Do preserve the solid-mint observed lane and the hatched-lilac synthetic lane with explicit labels.
Do retain the 3px orange, 4px-offset keyboard focus treatment and reduced-motion overrides.
Do pair visual summaries with their native table alternative and provenance record.
Do use red only for warnings, limitations, and unavailable evidence.
donts: Don't use rounded cards, pill controls, drop shadows, glass effects, or decorative gradients.
Don't rely on color alone to distinguish public observed evidence from synthetic demonstrations.
Don't use Newsreader for metadata, controls, navigation, or dense evidence text.
Don't make old public evidence look current, or synthetic planning output look observed.
Don't present descriptive attribution as causal proof.
